notes: The parts list matched 'Raspberry Pi' to pi-pico, but the circuit image shows a full-size Raspberry Pi with a 40-pin GPIO header (GPIO14, GPIO15, GPIO4, GND), so a new type 'raspberry-pi' was created.

Breadboard port names follow the catalogue (bank 't' = rows a-e, 'b' = rows f-j). The image is drawn with rows f-j at the top and a-e at the bottom, so the LED/resistor sit in the 't' bank and the blue ground rail next to rows a-e is called 'tn'.
Rail hole numbers (tn.1, tn.10, tn.19, tn.25) are estimated from the image; the rail is one strip so the numbers do not change connectivity.

Buttons: the text says legs in rows H and J; the wires sit in row F of the same column strips. Side 1 of each button is the column that goes to GND (col 1 / col 30); side 2 goes to GPIO14 (col 3) / GPIO15 (col 28). No external pull-up resistors, the gpiozero Button uses internal pull-ups.
LED long leg (anode) in column 16, short leg (cathode) in column 15, with the 330 ohm resistor from column 15 to the GND rail. Red wire from column 16 to GPIO4.

Pin-to-socket wires: port a is the socket (female) end on the Pi header, port b is the pin (male) end on the breadboard. The GND wire uses the GND pin directly beside GPIO4 (physical pin 9, named GND.2).
